recipes.name: Slow Cooker Chicken Pot Pie Stew
ingredients_raw: 4 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into cubes
2 (26 ounce) cans condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Combine potatoes, chicken, condensed soup, carrots, celery, bouillon, pepper, garlic salt, and celery salt in a slow cooker; cover and cook on High for 5 hours.
Stir in frozen mixed vegetables; continue to cook on High for 1 hour more.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Chicken Pot Pie Stew
raw_recipe.description: This slow cooker chicken pot pie is a hearty and comforting stew with tender chicken, potatoes, and vegetables in a rich, creamy sauce.

review.reviewBody: Just by reading this recipe I knew I was not going to add any salt to it. Ended up putting in garlic, pepper, and fresh basil. Also, instead of any buillon I added a can of chicken broth. I know the potatoes would have been good, but I put in wheat egg noodles. Also added onions and mushrooms. I will try the potatoes next time. Very easy, creamy and yummy.

The was really excellent, with a few small changes. As others suggested, I omitted the bouillon and used 1 can of low-sodium chicken broth. I also combine about 1/4 cup flour with some water and added to the dish during the last 15 minutes of cooking. Turned out nice and thick to spoon over our biscuits! I will definitely be keeping this recipe for the next time we want chicken and biscuits!

I substituted 6 cubes of bouillon with 2 tbsp Better Than Bouillon. The flavor was much better and richer without the added salt. I also used the tiny potatoes instead of the larger red potatoes. I also added mushrooms and sliced onion.

Very flavorful. I prefer my chicken shredded for things like this and only had frozen breasts. I used my pressure cooker for the frozen chicken, shredded it, then added it halfway through to the crockpot. The whole baby carrots were not done enough for my liking per the instructions. Next time I will omit them since the mixed veggies have carrots. I also had half the potatoes on hand that it called for but I wasn’t disappointed with not having enough. I honestly thought the amount of pepper listed was a mistake so I used half, which ended up being perfect. I think if I used the amount called for that it would have been too much. This is definitely a new go to recipe and can easily be used with ingredients I usually have on hand anyway.

I followed recipe to a tee - almost gave 3 stars because of the seasonings, but the base recipe is good, so it’s 4. Toooo much salt (and we’re salt freaks) and waaaay too much pepper. Next time I will use regular garlic powder and celery powder - not the salted kind for either one. One teaspoon of pepper would have been more than plenty. Really lovely dish, it’s just the salted seasonings and the pepper were over the top. With those adjustments, this will be a keeper. I served over southern buttermilk biscuits.

I changed the celery salt with organic herb salt. Made a homemade roux with chicken broth and cream instead of using processed food chicken soup. Having the standard serving size be 16 is a lot. Make it for 4 or 8 and people can double it if needed.

This was a big hit at a pot luck supper, served over mashed potatoes. My changes: add 2 tablespoons sour cream at the end after cooking; reduce bouillon cubes to 3, add a third can of cream of chicken soup, only 1 tsp garlic salt not 2, and no celery salt. I also used frozen peas instead of mixed vegetables. When serving over mashed potatoes I used a few less potatoes and a little extra chicken.

Instead of using canned soup (I had none on hand), I made in just a few minutes a homemade cream soup that was so rich and creamy! I also had full fat chicken broth in the freezer from other chicken recipes started in my magical crockpot. Both made this a bigger hit! We don't eat a lot of baked goods, so I skipped bread. If looking for some carbs, just add more veggies. Soooo yummy especially since weather just turned to the 60degree highs and 40 degree lows. Perfect.

This is now our favorite dish! But, I did make a few changes. When at the store I saw Campbell's Cream of Chicken with Herbs and used that. Instead of celery salt, I added chopped celery and instead of garlic salt, I used real garlic. (So much sodium in the canned soup so I wanted to eliminate adding additional salt.) I also added chopped onion and used corn and peas instead of the mixed veggies.

This was incredible. I added 1 1/4 cups of culinary chIcken broth, and added some garlic powder and basil. Thickened it a bit with a tablespoon of corn starch mixed with about a half cup of the hot sauce mixture, just before adding the frozen vegetables. We got six adult size servings. Delicious. Will make again.

Love this recipe!! It’s my second time making it. My husband loves it , and so do I! I used did fresh vegetables for the celery, broccoli and carrots. I added canned corn and peas in the last hour and a half. I also added mini red potatoes cut in quarters. I used chicken tenderloins instead of chicken breasts. So good!! You really can make it to your liking. Highly recommend!

After reading the reviews and the tweaks, I too made a few changes. I left the added salts out and instead of the mixed vegetables, I added a cup each of frozen corn, lima beans and peas, along with mushrooms. I also added a cup of chicken stock. I cooked on high for 3 hours then turned on low for 4 hours. Everything was done to perfection. I served it over flaky biscuits and it was a crowd pleaser. Definitely a keeper.
All the veggies give this so much flavor! We didn't need biscuits because the potatoes in it are so filling. Will make it again!

I made the recipe pretty much as directed, but I cut it in half because it's just my wife and me. I used two 10.5 oz cans of soup because that's what I had. I used the bullion cube, although I cut it in half. I accidentally forgot to cut the amount of celery in half, but it was fine. When I added the frozen vegetables at the end, I also added about a half cup of water, to make up for the 5 oz of missing soup. The consistency and taste of the finished product was great, although maybe a tad too peppery. If I were to make it again, I might add some onions and reduce the amount of black pepper. Halving the recipe made enough for two dinners for me and my wife, with a little left over for another lunch portion. I don't think the full recipe would feed 16.
I absolutely love hardy stews and soups, so my lovely wife prepared this stew for me, and it was amazing! Definitely a family keeper.

A delicious meal, 2 or 3 for my wife and I, during these colder months. I bought a fresh loaf of French bread to go along with it, although I also bought the rolls, for later I guess. Not a difficult recipe to prepare, especially with a crock pot. My wife did suggest that next time perhaps I either marinate the chicken first or buy a rotisserie chicken that they sell at the grocery store. She still ate it all without that so I guess it was ok.

We cook low sodium, so I used four 10.5 oz cans of unsalted soup and sprinkled seasoned salt at the table to taste. Instead of frozen veggies I added more carrots and celery. (Cook time was five hours without the extra hour for frozen veggies. Test chicken for doneness.) A can of peas might be nice to add next time and fewer potatoes next --or smaller ones. Ten medium taters was a LOT. We had enough for eight decent portions! I froze some. Winter is coming...!
Too much potato and not enough chicken. I had to add water to the slow cooker.

This is delicious! Takes more than 20 minutes to prep… as most things never accurately predict or maybe I’m slow! I followed everything except: didn’t have two 26 oz cans of cream of chicken so I used what I had, 3 cans cream of chicken, one cream of celery and one cream of potato, all10.5 ounces. I don’t have garlic SALT so I used 1 1/2 t Adobe seasoning and 1/2 t garlic powder, also omitted the bouillon cube.. I omitted celery salt because I used the cream of celery soup. I had 12 oz bag of frozen mixed vegetables and I used about half bag of frozen peas and carrots. I used golden potatoes cut in quarters. The pepper was fine but I saw a lot of comments after I made it but it didn’t seem too bad, maybe I didn’t measure two full teaspoons. I served my bowl over top a Pillsbury buttermilk biscuit and I love this! I think the recipe is very versatile and easy to swap things for what you have on hand. It completely filled my crockpot to the top and I’m glad I used my big oblong crockpot. Saving this recipe for future, especially potlucks or big family get togethers.
I loved it. I'm going to see how it freezes. I made this again but I used cream of mushroom soup. I totally love this
